21. Data Security for Data Engineers数据工程师的数据安全

Katharine Jarmul

凯瑟琳·贾穆尔

Is your data safe? What about the data you process every day? How do you know? Can you guarantee it?

你的数据安全吗？你每天处理的数据呢？你怎么知道？你能保证吗？

These questions aren't meant to send you running in fear. Instead, I want you to approach security pragmatically. As data engineers, we're often managing the most valuable company resource. For this reason, it only makes sense that we learn and apply security engineering to our work.

这些问题不是要把你吓得落荒而逃。相反，我希望你务实地看待安全问题。作为数据工程师，我们常常在管理公司最有价值的资源。因此，学习并把安全工程应用到我们的工作中，是再自然不过的事。

How can we do so? Here are a few tips.

我们该怎么做？下面是几条建议。

Learn About Security学习安全知识

Most data engineers come from either a computer science or a data science background, so you may not have had exposure to computer and network security concepts. Learn about them by attending security conferences, meetups, and other events. Read up on security best practices for the particular architecture or infrastructure you use. Chat with the IT/DevOps or security folks at your company to hear what measures are already in place. I'm not asking you to become an expert, but I do want you to be informed.

大多数数据工程师要么出身计算机科学，要么出身数据科学，可能没接触过计算机和网络安全概念。通过参加安全会议、线下聚会和其他活动来学习。读一下你所用架构或基础设施的安全最佳实践。和公司里 IT/DevOps 或安全团队的人聊一聊，听听已经有哪些防护措施。我不是要你成为专家，但我希望你心里有数。

Monitor, Log, and Test Access监控、记录并测试访问

Monitor, log, and track access to the machines or containers you use, to the databases or other data repositories you maintain, and to the code and processing systems you contribute to daily. Make sure only credentialed users or machines can access these systems. Create firewall rules (yes, even in the cloud and even with containers) and test them by using a port scanner or ping sweep. Monitor and alert on any unusual access or network behavior.

对你使用的机器或容器、你维护的数据库或其他数据仓库、你每天贡献代码的处理系统，都要做访问监控、日志记录和跟踪。确保只有经过授权的用户或机器才能访问这些系统。创建防火墙规则（没错，哪怕在云上、哪怕用容器），并用端口扫描器或 ping 扫描来测试。对任何异常访问或网络行为进行监控和告警。

— p.60 —

Encrypt Data加密数据

Making sure sensitive data is protected should be one of the key things we do as data engineers. Whenever possible, encrypt data or sensitive fields—both at rest and in transit. According to IBM's 2019 Cost of a Data Breach Report, this is one of the best ways to prevent a costly data breach.

确保敏感数据受到保护，应当是数据工程师的核心职责之一。只要可能，就要对数据或敏感字段加密——无论是静态存储还是传输中。根据 IBM 2019 年《数据泄露成本报告》，这是防止代价高昂的数据泄露的最佳方式之一。

Automate Security Tests自动化安全测试

Already using CI/CD as part of your data engineering? (If not, please stop reading and go do that right now.) Implement security tests as a part of that deployment. This can be as simple as testing bad credentials, testing for encryption, and testing that the latest security updates for your libraries are being used. The more you automate this testing and can stop and alert for any potential security threats, the safer your processing and pipelines will be.

已经在数据工程中用 CI/CD 了吗？（如果没有，请停止阅读，马上去搭。）把安全测试作为部署流程的一部分。简单到可以是：测试错误凭据能否登录、测试是否加密、测试你所用库是否用了最新安全更新。你把这种测试自动化得越好，越能在潜在安全威胁面前停下来并告警，你的处理流程和管道就越安全。

Ask for Help寻求帮助

If you are lucky enough to have a security team, ask them to help you assess the security of the processing infrastructure, networks, and scripts. If not, see when your company's next external security review is scheduled and ask for time to talk with the experts about measures you can take to provide better security for your data engineering.

如果你足够幸运有一个安全团队，请他们帮你评估处理基础设施、网络和脚本的安全性。如果没有，查一下公司下一次外部安全评审安排在什么时候，并争取时间与专家聊聊，看看你能采取哪些措施来更好地保护你的数据工程。

This can include pen-testing of data collection endpoints or exposed APIs you use or maintain, or simply a security review of the processing deployment, monitoring, and architecture. Either way, getting expert advice will likely make you feel more confident about the measures you have and those you want to prioritize or implement in the future.

这可以包括对你使用或维护的数据采集端点、对外暴露 API 做渗透测试，或者只是对处理部署、监控和架构做一次安全评审。无论哪种方式，获得专家建议都会让你对现有措施、以及未来想优先或落地的措施更有信心。

For your particular role or company, there may be even more low-hanging security fruit. Scheduling a regular security sprint into your planning is a great way to stay on top of these issues and improve security over time. When faced with those questions again, you and your team can respond with ease of mind, knowing your data-engineering workflows are secure.

在你特定的岗位或公司，可能还有更多唾手可得的安全改进点。在规划里排一个定期的安全冲刺，是跟踪这些问题、持续改进安全的好办法。当再次面对那些问题时，你和你的团队就可以安心作答——因为你们知道自己的数据工程工作流是安全的。

— p.61 —

22. Data Validation Is More Than Summary Statistics数据校验不只是汇总统计

Emily Riederer

艾米丽·里德勒

Which of these numbers doesn't belong? –1, 0, 1, NA.

下面这些数中哪个格格不入？–1、0、1、NA。

It may be hard to tell. If the data in question should be non-negative, –1 is clearly wrong; if it should be complete, the NA is problematic; if it represents the signs to be used in summation, 0 is questionable. In short, there is no data quality without data context.

可能很难分辨。如果相关数据应当非负，–1 显然是错的；如果应当完整，NA 就有问题；如果它表示求和时用的符号，0 就可疑。一句话：没有数据上下文，就没有数据质量。

Data-quality management is widely recognized as a critical component of data engineering. However, while the need for always-on validation is uncontroversial, approaches vary widely. Too often, these approaches rely solely on summary statistics or basic, univariate anomaly-detection methods that are easily automated and widely scalable. However, in the long run, context-free data-quality checks ignore the nuance and help us detect more-pernicious errors that may go undetected by downstream users.

数据质量管理被公认为数据工程的关键组成。然而，虽然“需要始终在线的校验”这一点毫无争议，但具体做法千差万别。太多时候，这些做法只依赖汇总统计或基础的单变量异常检测方法——这些方法容易自动化、可大规模扩展。然而长期来看，脱离上下文的数据质量检查忽略了细微差别，反而会让我们漏掉那些更隐蔽、下游用户可能发现不了的错误。

Defining context-enriched business rules as checks on data quality can complement statistical approaches to data validation by encoding domain knowledge. Instead of just defining high-level requirements (e.g., "non-null"), we can define expected interactions between different fields in our data (e.g., "lifetime payments are less than lifetime purchases for each ecommerce customer").

把富含上下文的业务规则定义为数据质量检查，可以把领域知识编码进去，作为对统计式数据校验的补充。我们不只是定义高层要求（例如“非空”），还可以定义数据中不同字段之间应有的相互关系（例如“对每个电商客户，历史累计付款应小于历史累计购买额”）。

This enables the exploration of internal consistency across fields in one or more datasets—not just the reasonableness of any given field in isolation—and allows us to validate that the data produced concurs with the true business intent (e.g., the aforementioned check is definitely true only if we are considering gross purchases and deducting any returns). While these checks can still be simple arithmetic, they encode a level of intuition that no autonomous approach could hope to find (e.g., the need to compare running totals of select metrics after grouping the data at the customer level) and ask questions that might be more representative of the way our ETL process could break (e.g., by loading payments multiple times).

这让我们能够探查一个或多个数据集中字段间的内部一致性——而不只是孤立地看某个字段是否合理——并校验产出的数据是否符合真实业务意图（例如，前面那条检查只有在我们看的是毛购买额、并扣除退货时才必然成立）。这些检查虽然仍是简单的算术，却编码了任何自动化方法都不可能自己发现的直觉层次（例如，需要在客户层级分组后再比较某些指标的累计值），并提出那些更能代表 ETL 流程可能以何种方式坏掉的问题（例如，付款被重复加载）。

— p.62 —

Business-rule data checks can further exploit unique human knowledge about the data structures that might not be fully evident from the data itself. For example, if we are working with repeated measures (panel) data for a consistent set of subjects, many intended unique keys or expected trends may exist within each subject but not across the whole dataset; alternatively, if we are working with hierarchical data, checks can explore the appropriate "nesting" of these levels.

业务规则数据检查还能利用关于数据结构的、独特的人类知识——这些知识从数据本身看并不那么显然。例如，如果我们在处理一组固定对象的重复测量（面板）数据，许多预期唯一键或预期趋势可能存在于每个对象内部，但不存在于整个数据集上；反之，如果我们在处理层级数据，检查可以探查这些层级是否被正确“嵌套”。

While context-enriched checks on data quality can help provide a more robust and nuanced validation of data quality, there is no free lunch. The major downside of this approach is that it may require a significant amount of manual work from both the business and engineering teams to define and implement such conditions. As such, developers must carefully prioritize where to invest limited resources. However, even adding these checks to particularly critical subsets of fields or especially error-prone steps in a pipeline (major transformations or combinations of diverse sources) can go a long way toward promoting a more holistic approach to data quality.

富含上下文的数据质量检查有助于提供更稳健、更细致的校验，但天下没有免费的午餐。这种方法的主要缺点是：业务团队和工程团队都要投入大量手工工作来定义和实现这些条件。因此开发者必须谨慎地决定把有限资源投在哪里。然而，哪怕只是把这些检查加到特别关键的字段子集、或管道中特别容易出错的步骤（重大转换、多源合并）上，也能大大推动一种更整体的数据质量观。

— p.63 —

23. Data Warehouses Are the Past, Present, and Future数据仓库的过去、现在与未来

James Densmore

詹姆斯·登斯莫尔

The death of the data warehouse, long prophesied, seems to be always on the horizon yet never realized. First it was NoSQL, then Hadoop, then data lakes that would kill the data warehouse. Yet here we are. Snowflake was the hottest initial public offering (IPO) of 2020, and the demand for data and analytics engineers who can crank value out of a data warehouse is as high as ever.

“数据仓库已死”的预言流传已久，似乎总在地平线上却从未成真。先是 NoSQL，再是 Hadoop，然后是数据湖——都被认为会干掉数据仓库。然而我们还在这儿。Snowflake 是 2020 年最火的 IPO，市场对能从数据仓库中榨出价值的数据与分析工程师的需求前所未有地高。

In 2010, the future of data warehouses felt pretty bleak. Most analytics teams were relying on traditional row-based, online transactional processing (OLTP) databases for their data warehouses. Data volume was exploding. When it came to processing and querying all that data for analysis, columnar databases came to the rescue, but they required expanding hardware. While data warehouse bare-metal appliances provided a massive jump in processing power, it was quite an investment to add the hardware to your server room. It's unimaginable 10 years later.

2010 年时，数据仓库的未来看起来相当黯淡。大多数分析团队还在用传统的行式联机事务处理（OLTP）数据库作为数据仓库。数据量在爆炸式增长。当要处理和查询这么多数据做分析时，列式数据库救了场，但那需要扩容硬件。数据仓库的裸机一体机虽然带来处理能力的巨大飞跃，但要往机房里堆硬件，是一笔不小的投入。放到 10 年后的今天看简直难以想象。

Things changed for the better in 2012, when Amazon launched Redshift, a columnar data warehouse that you could spin up in minutes and pay for in small increments with no massive up-front cost, built on top of PostgreSQL. Migrations away from overtaxed, row-based SQL data warehouses to Redshift grew massively. The barrier to entry for a high-performing data warehouse was lowered substantially, and suddenly what looked like the impending death of the warehouses was a rebirth.

2012 年事情好转了：Amazon 推出了 Redshift——一个基于 PostgreSQL 构建的列式数据仓库，几分钟就能拉起，按小步长计费，不需要巨额前期投入。从不堪重负的行式 SQL 数据仓库向 Redshift 的大规模迁移由此开始。高性能数据仓库的入门门槛大幅降低，眼看就要到来的“仓库之死”突然变成了重生。

Next, extract, load, transform (ELT) wiped out extract, transform, load (ETL). The difference between the two patterns is where the T (transform) step takes place, and distributed columnar databases made it all possible. It's now better to focus on extracting data and loading it into a data warehouse, and then performing the necessary transformations. With ELT, data

接着，抽取-加载-转换（ELT）模式干掉了抽取-转换-加载（ETL）模式。两者的区别在于 T（转换）步骤发生在哪里，而分布式列式数据库让这一切成为可能。现在更好的做法是：专注于抽取数据并加载进数据仓库，然后再做必要的转换。借助 ELT，数据

— p.64 —

engineers can focus on the extract and load steps, while analysts can utilize SQL to transform the data that's been ingested for reporting and analysis.

工程师可以专注于抽取和加载，分析师则用 SQL 对已接入的数据做转换，用于报表和分析。

In other words, this new breed of data warehouses made it possible (and economical) to store and query far higher volumes of data than ever before. ELT saved the data warehouse.

换句话说，这种新型数据仓库让存储和查询比以往大得多的数据量成为可能（而且经济上划算）。ELT 拯救了数据仓库。

The concept of a data lake was first introduced in 2011. The benefit of storing vast amounts of data without having to define its structure when it's stored (schema-on-write), but rather when it's queried (schema-on-read), is real. However, there's a cost to such an approach when it comes to data discovery and governance, as well as in complexity for the data analytics or analytics engineer who works with the data.

数据湖的概念最早在 2011 年提出。存储海量数据时不需要在写入时定义结构（schema-on-write），而是在查询时再定义（schema-on-read），这种好处是真实的。然而，这种做法在数据发现和治理、以及对使用数据的分析工程师的复杂度上，是有代价的。

With the cost of storing and querying large structured datasets dropping and the performance spiking upward, some of the downsides of data lakes for analytics became more noticeable. Still, data lakes have a place in an analytics infrastructure. There's still a need to store data that's not consistently structured, or in a volume that makes even the most robust data warehouses creak. However, for most data teams, data lakes have been a complement to their data warehouse rather than a replacement.

随着存储和查询大型结构化数据集的成本下降、性能飙升，数据湖用于分析的一些缺点变得更明显。尽管如此，数据湖在分析基础设施中仍有一席之地。仍有必要存储那些结构不一致、或大到让最稳健的数据仓库都吱呀作响的数据量。然而对大多数数据团队而言，数据湖是数据仓库的补充，而非替代。

Data warehouses aren't going anywhere anytime soon. Snowflake continues to blow away expectations for developers and investors alike, and I expect a wave of data warehouse innovation in the near future.

数据仓库短期内不会消失。Snowflake 持续超出开发者和投资者的预期，我预计不远的将来会有一波数据仓库创新浪潮。

For those hesitant to invest in a greenfield data warehouse, migrate a legacy one to a modern platform, or hire data engineers with data warehousing know-how, don't fear! You're building for now and investing intelligently for the future.

那些还在犹豫是否要建一个全新数据仓库、把遗留仓库迁移到现代平台、或招聘有数据仓库经验的数据工程师的人，别害怕！你既是在为当下建设，也是在为未来明智下注。

— p.65 —

24. Defining and Managing Messages in Log-Centric Architectures以日志为中心的架构中的消息定义与管理

Boris Lublinsky

鲍里斯·卢布林斯基

Messaging systems are changing the way we are exposing data. Instead of focusing on the API between a producer and consumer, we have to focus on the message definitions.

消息系统正在改变我们对外暴露数据的方式。我们不再专注于生产方与消费方之间的 API，而必须专注于消息定义。

With logs becoming a centerpiece of the architecture, they are starting to take on the role of an enterprise data backbone, somewhat similar to the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) for streaming systems. This architecture encourages the creation of canonical data models, because schema enforcement avoids many problems (e.g., typing errors). This is not a new idea—compare it to the canonical data model used in enterprise application integration (EAI) and service-oriented architecture (SOA), and the concept of standardized service contracts. The rationale is the same in both cases, and this approach is identical to the EAI canonical messaging pattern, ensuring that the content of the log will be understood by all participants.

随着日志成为架构的核心，它们开始承担企业数据骨干网的角色，有点类似于 HDFS 之于流式系统。这种架构鼓励创建规范化数据模型，因为强制 schema 可以避免许多问题（例如类型错误）。这不是什么新想法——可以对照企业应用集成（EAI）和面向服务架构（SOA）中使用的规范化数据模型，以及标准化服务契约的概念。两者的原理相同，这种做法与 EAI 的规范化消息模式一致，确保日志的内容能被所有参与方理解。

The canonical data model provides an additional level of decoupling between each service's individual data format and simplifies data mapping among internal models of different services. If a new service is added to the implementation, only a transformation between the canonical data model and the internal model is required, independent of how this data is represented by other services using it.

规范化数据模型在各服务自身数据格式之间提供了额外一层解耦，并简化了不同服务内部模型间的数据映射。如果在实现中加入一个新服务，只需要在规范化数据模型和它的内部模型之间做一次转换，而与其他使用该数据的服务如何表示该数据无关。

Ideally, this canonical data model should never change, but in reality it does. In these cases, you should strive for backward compatibility when making changes to message schemas for services that produce messages. Sometimes breaking changes are unavoidable. In this case, existing consumers of the given message schema are at risk of breaking.

理想情况下，这个规范化数据模型永远不该变，但现实中它会变。在这种情况下，对生产消息的服务做消息 schema 变更时，应尽量保持向后兼容。有时破坏性变更不可避免。这时，该消息 schema 的既有消费方就有出问题的风险。

A solution to this problem, similar to API versioning best practices, is creation of a new deployment of the service with a new topic. Consumers that

这个问题的一个解决方案——类似于 API 版本管理最佳实践——是为服务创建一个带新 topic 的新部署。支持

— p.66 —

support the new schema can consume messages from this topic, while the ones that assume an old schema will continue to leverage existing ones.

新 schema 的消费方从这个新 topic 消费消息，而那些仍假设旧 schema 的消费方继续使用既有 topic。

This approach to versioning allows functionality to evolve independently without breaking the rest of the system. A downside of this approach is increased size and complexity of the overall system, caused by multiple deployments of the same service with different versions. To prevent this from happening, it is important to introduce a version-deprecation policy; old versions should be deleted after a set time period.

这种版本管理方式让功能可以独立演进，而不破坏系统其他部分。缺点是：同一服务的多个不同版本部署会让整个系统变得更大、更复杂。为防止这一点，重要的是引入版本弃用策略；旧版本应在设定时间后删除。

Message design and management are important components of log-centric architecture. To build your system correctly, make sure that you leverage the following:

消息设计与管理是日志中心架构的重要组成。要正确地构建系统，请确保利用好以下两点：

  • A well-defined semantic data model that is the foundation of your message definitions.
    一个定义良好的语义数据模型，作为你消息定义的基础。
  • A well-defined strategy allowing easy creation and deletion of topics to support versioning. It is also recommended to directly encode a version identifier into the topic name.
    一个定义良好的策略，让 topic 的创建和删除都容易进行，以支持版本管理。还建议把版本号直接编码进 topic 名。
— p.67 —

25. Demystify the Source and Illuminate the Data Pipeline弄清源头、照亮数据管道

Meghan Kwartler

梅根·夸特勒

You've been assigned to a new project, new team, or new company. You want to dig in and make an impact to add business value. It can be tempting to start writing code immediately, but if you resist the inclination to make initial assumptions and instead give your attention to setting up a solid foundation, it will pay dividends moving forward.

你被派到一个新项目、新团队或新公司。你想扎进去、做出影响、增添业务价值。立刻动手写代码很诱人，但如果你忍住“先做初步假设”的冲动，转而把精力放在打牢基础上，未来会获得回报。

First, discover where and how the data originates. When your data is initiated from users, it is useful to get their perspective on their entry experience. Each time I walk the floor of a manufacturing plant or talk to a machine operator about how they use a system, I gain valuable knowledge. Often I discover ways users are entering data that are inconsistent with the original system design, or the valid reasons why they are omitting data. If you don't have access to the people entering data, study their training documentation and talk to the business analysts associated with that function.

首先，搞清楚数据从哪里来、怎么来。当数据由用户发起时，了解他们录入时的体验很有帮助。每次我走在制造车间里、或与机器操作员聊他们如何使用系统时，都能获得宝贵知识。我常常发现用户录入数据的方式与系统原始设计不一致，或者发现他们漏录数据的合理原因。如果你接触不到录入数据的人，就研究他们的培训文档，并与对应职能的业务分析师聊聊。

Get to know the specifications when your data originates from sensors, equipment, or hardware. Dig into the manuals and documentation to clarify how the data is generated. You will then have a clear understanding when you encounter this data later in your analysis. Knowing the expected values also helps you identify possible malfunctions in the source equipment.

当数据来自传感器、设备或硬件时，去了解它们的规格。翻一翻手册和文档，弄清楚数据是怎么产生的。这样在你后续分析中遇到这些数据时，就会有清晰的理解。知道预期值还有助于你识别源设备可能的故障。

Now examine the metadata. You have discovered the originating business events for implicit, explicit, manually entered, or automatically generated data. Descriptive metadata accompanies each of these sources. For example, metadata includes equipment event timestamps, device types, or descriptive user data. Determine whether this metadata from numerous sources is consistent and could be unified. For instance, timestamp formatting may differ across time zones.

现在检查元数据。你已经发现了隐性、显性、手工录入或自动生成数据所源自的业务事件。每一种来源都伴随描述性元数据。例如元数据包括设备事件时间戳、设备类型或描述性用户数据。判断来自众多源的这些元数据是否一致、能否统一。例如，不同时区的时间戳格式可能不同。

— p.68 —

Now it's time to trace. Whether you've identified one or one hundred sources of data, how does that data move through the pipeline and arrive in the place where you will access it? Another consideration is that data types could be converted, and business translation may be required as data moves through systems.

现在该做追踪了。无论你识别出了一个还是一百个数据源，这些数据是如何流过管道、最终到达你将访问的位置的？另一个要考虑的是：数据在系统间移动时可能会做类型转换，也可能需要业务层面的翻译。

If you have the good fortune to receive this type of information during your onboarding, be extremely grateful and recognize that this documentation is a gift. It will set you up for success. Then reference it. Sometimes effort is made to develop valuable documentation, but more often it isn't utilized to its fullest capacity.

如果你足够幸运，在入职时就拿到这类信息，请万分感激，并认识到这份文档是一份礼物。它会为你的成功铺路。然后真的去用它。有时大家花力气写出了有价值的文档，但更多时候它没有被充分利用。

During your investigation, create documentation if it doesn't exist. It doesn't need to be overly complicated. It can be simple and yet make a strong impact at the same time. Pay it forward and help the next person who will be tasked with using data to benefit the business.

在你调研过程中，如果文档不存在，就动手写。它不必过于复杂，可以很简单，同时却能产生很大影响。把这份帮助传递下去，帮助下一个要靠数据为业务创造价值的人。

— p.69 —

26. Develop Communities, Not Just Code培养社区，而不只是写代码

Emily Riederer

艾米丽·里德勒

As a data engineer, you may think of your core job responsibility as building a data pipeline. In fact, that's probably what was laid out in your job description and how your value is measured by your manager. However, you're uniquely positioned to exercise a much greater impact on your organization if you think about developing a data culture along with your data products.

作为数据工程师，你可能把核心职责理解为搭建数据管道。事实上，这很可能就是岗位描述里写的、也是你经理衡量你价值的方式。然而，如果你在做数据产品的同时也想着培育数据文化，你就处在一个独特位置，能对组织产生大得多的影响。

The data you produce is likely consumed by countless data scientists, data analysts, and users spread across disparate lines of business. In large organizations, these individuals may be fragmented and unaware of similar questions they are asking and answering with the same core data assets. In this sense, your data is posed to be a shared platform that can connect a network of users with common objectives. Empowered users not only will derive more value from your data, but also may be able to self-service or crowd-source more of their data needs instead of continuing to rely on a data-engineering team for ad hoc requests.

你产出的数据，可能被分散在不同业务线的无数数据科学家、数据分析师和用户消费。在大型组织里，这些人可能彼此割裂，没意识到自己正在用同样的核心数据资产问着、答着相似的问题。从这个意义上说，你的数据完全可以成为一个共享平台，把一群目标一致的用户连成网络。被赋能的用户不仅能从你的数据中获得更多价值，还可能自助或众包地满足自己更多的数据需求，而不必继续依赖数据工程团队处理临时请求。

Such networks and communities won't arise without concerted effort. Downstream users are typically focused on obtaining answers to specific business and strategy questions and see data as a means to an end—not a central, binding force in an analytical ecosystem. Additionally, the data literacy and proficiency of data consumers across different tools may cause more fragmentation.

这样的网络和社区不会自动出现，需要同心协力。下游用户通常专注于得到某些具体业务和战略问题的答案，把数据视为达成目的的手段——而不是分析生态中一股核心的、有凝聚力的力量。此外，不同数据消费方在各种工具上的数据素养和熟练度，可能造成进一步的碎片化。

Data scientists may be adept at Spark or have all their code in Jupyter notebooks on GitHub, whereas line-of-business users might struggle with SQL and resort to dashboards, spreadsheets, or canned reports for their data needs. The confluence of tight timelines, matrixed organizations, and disparate tools leaves your users without a shared language or forum to find commonalities.

数据科学家可能精通 Spark，或把所有代码放在 GitHub 上的 Jupyter notebook 里；而业务线用户可能磕磕绊绊地写 SQL，转而用仪表盘、电子表格或固定报表来满足数据需求。紧张的工期、矩阵式组织、五花八门的工具搅在一起，让你的用户既没有共同语言，也没有一个论坛去发现共性。

— p.70 —

Here are some ways you can help foster a data community or practice:

下面是一些你可以用来培育数据社区或数据实践的方式：

  • Query usage logs and, when privacy permits, publish them to help users connect.
    查询使用日志，并在隐私允许的情况下公开发布，帮助用户互相连接。
  • Engage with users to understand what business questions bring them to your data and how they interact with it. This can be done in individual one-on-one user interviews or larger design sessions.
    与用户交流，理解是什么业务问题把他们带到你的数据面前、他们又是如何与数据交互的。可以通过一对一访谈或更大的设计讨论会进行。
  • Empower users by providing training and resources for them to engage with data in more advanced ways. Don't underestimate that what you perceive as basic skills could be transformative. For example, teaching a marketing team basic SQL or training data scientists in Airflow could help these teams automate parts of their workflows.
    通过提供培训和资源来赋能用户，让他们能用更高级的方式与数据打交道。别低估你眼中的“基础技能”——它可能带来变革。例如，教市场团队基础 SQL、或培训数据科学家使用 Airflow，可以帮助这些团队把部分工作流自动化。
  • Share as much of your work as possible (e.g., scripts that are part of your ETL pipeline) to help more-advanced users learn and reuse them.
    尽可能多地分享你的工作（例如 ETL 管道中的脚本），帮助更高级的用户学习和复用。
  • Build centralized tools that help users consume data, and open them to community contribution.
    构建帮助用户消费数据的集中式工具，并向社区贡献开放。
— p.71 —

27. Effective Data Engineering in the Cloud World云时代的高效数据工程

Dipti Borkar (VP of Product, Alluxio)

迪普蒂·博卡（Alluxio 产品副总裁）

The cloud has changed the dynamics of data engineering as well as the behavior of data engineers in many ways. This is primarily because a data engineer on premises deals only with databases and some parts of the Hadoop stack. In the cloud, things are a bit different.

云计算在很多方面改变了数据工程的面貌，也改变了数据工程师的行为。这主要是因为：在本地机房，数据工程师只与数据库和 Hadoop 栈的某些部分打交道。在云上，事情不太一样了。

Data engineers suddenly need to think differently and more broadly. Instead of being focused purely on data infrastructure, you are now almost a full-stack engineer (leaving out the final end application, perhaps). Skills are increasingly needed across the broader stack—compute, containers, storage, data movement, performance, network. Here are some design concepts and data stack elements to keep in mind.

数据工程师突然需要换一种、更广阔的思路。你不再只专注于数据基础设施，而几乎成了一个全栈工程师（也许除了最终端的应用）。整个更广的栈都越来越需要技能——计算、容器、存储、数据移动、性能、网络。下面是一些要牢记的设计概念和数据栈要素。

Disaggregated Data Stack解耦的数据栈

Historically, databases were tightly integrated, with all core components built together. Hadoop changed that with colocated computing and storage in a distributed system instead of being in a single or a few boxes. Then the cloud changed that. Today, it is a fully disaggregated stack with each core element of the database management system being its own layer. Pick each component wisely.

历史上，数据库是紧耦合的，所有核心组件构建在一起。Hadoop 改变了这一点：它把计算和存储放在分布式系统中协同，而不是在单机或少数几台机器里。然后云又改变了这一点。今天，这是一个完全解耦的栈——数据库管理系统的每个核心要素都是独立的一层。请明智地选择每个组件。

Orchestrate, Orchestrate, Orchestrate编排、编排、再编排

The cloud has created a need for and enabled mass orchestration—whether that's Kubernetes for containers, Alluxio for data, Istio for APIs, Kafka for events, or Terraform for scripting.

云催生了大规模编排的需求，也使之成为可能——无论是容器的 Kubernetes、数据的 Alluxio、API 的 Istio、事件的 Kafka，还是脚本化的 Terraform。

Efficiency dramatically increases through abstraction and orchestration. Because a data engineer for the cloud now has full-stack concerns, orchestration can be a data engineer's best-kept secret.

通过抽象和编排，效率会大幅提升。因为云上的数据工程师现在要操心全栈，编排可以说是数据工程师最大的秘密武器。

— p.72 —

Copying Data Creates Problems拷贝数据会制造问题

Fundamentally, after data lands in the enterprise, it should not be copied around except, of course, for backup, recovery, and disaster-recovery scenarios. How to make this data accessible to as many business units, data scientists, and analysts as possible with as few new copies created as possible is the data engineer's puzzle to solve. This is where in the legacy DBMS world a buffer pool helped, making sure the compute (query engine) always had access to data stored in a consistent, optimized way in a format that was suitable for the query engine to process, rather than a format optimized for storage. Technologies like Alluxio can dramatically simplify this, bringing data closer to compute and making it more performant and accessible.

从根本上说，数据落到企业之后，就不该被到处拷贝——当然备份、恢复和容灾场景除外。如何让尽可能多的业务部门、数据科学家和分析师都能访问这些数据，同时尽量不产生新副本，是数据工程师要解的题。在传统 DBMS 世界里，缓冲池（buffer pool）就帮过这个忙：它确保计算层（查询引擎）始终能访问到以一致、优化方式存储的数据，且格式适合查询引擎处理，而不是为存储优化的格式。像 Alluxio 这样的技术可以大大简化这件事——把数据带得离计算更近，让它性能更好、更容易访问。

S3 CompatibilityS3 兼容性

Because of the popularity of Amazon S3, object stores in general will be the next dominant storage systems—at least for a few years (a five- to eight-year cycle, typically). Think ahead and choose a storage tier that will last for some time. S3-compatible object stores should be your primary choice. While they are not great at all data-driven workloads, many technologies help remove their deficiencies.

由于 Amazon S3 的流行，对象存储总体上将成为下一个主导的存储系统——至少持续几年（通常是 5 到 8 年一个周期）。往前看，选择一个能撑一段时间的存储层。S3 兼容的对象存储应当是你的首选。虽然它们并不擅长所有数据驱动型工作负载，但有许多技术能弥补其不足。

SQL and Structured Data Are Still InSQL 和结构化数据依然流行

While SQL has existed since the 1970s, it still is the easiest way for analysts to understand and do something with data. AI models will continue to evolve, but SQL has lasted for close to 50 years. Pick two, or at most three, frameworks to bet on and invest in—but build a platform that will over time support as many as needed. Currently, Presto is turning into a popular SQL query engine choice for the disaggregated stack.

虽然 SQL 从 1970 年代就存在，它仍然是分析师理解数据、用数据做事的最简单方式。AI 模型会持续演进，但 SQL 已经存在了近 50 年。挑两个、最多三个框架下注并投入——但要构建一个长期能按需支持任意多框架的平台。目前，Presto 正在成为解耦栈中受欢迎的 SQL 查询引擎选择。

— p.73 —

28. Embrace the Data Lake Architecture拥抱数据湖架构

Vinoth Chandar

维诺特·钱达

Oftentimes, data engineers build data pipelines to extract data from external sources, transform it, and enable other parts of the organization to query the resulting datasets. While it's easier in the short term to just build all of this as a single-stage pipeline, a more thoughtful data architecture is needed to scale this model to thousands of datasets spanning multiple tera/petabytes.

数据工程师常常搭建数据管道，从外部源抽取数据、做转换，然后让组织的其他部分查询产出的数据集。虽然短期内把这一切做成单阶段管道更省事，但要把这种模式扩展到数千个数据集、横跨数 TB/PB 规模，就需要一种更考究的数据架构。

Common Pitfalls常见陷阱

Let's understand some common pitfalls with the single-stage approach. First of all, it limits scalability since the input data to such a pipeline is obtained by scanning upstream databases—relational database management systems (RDBMSs) or NoSQL stores—that would ultimately stress these systems and even result in outages. Further, accessing such data directly allows for little standardization across pipelines (e.g., standard timestamp, key fields) and increases the risk of data breakages due to lack of schemas/data contracts. Finally, not all data or columns are available in a single place, to freely cross-correlate them for insights or design machine learning models.

我们来理解一下单阶段方式的常见陷阱。首先，它限制了可扩展性，因为这种管道的输入数据是通过扫描上游数据库——关系数据库管理系统（RDBMS）或 NoSQL 存储——获得的，最终会压垮这些系统甚至导致故障。其次，直接访问这些数据使得跨管道几乎没有标准化（例如统一时间戳、键字段），并因为缺乏 schema/数据契约而增加数据损坏的风险。最后，并不是所有数据或字段都在同一个地方，可以自由地交叉关联以获得洞见或设计机器学习模型。

Data Lakes数据湖

In recent years, the data lake architecture has grown in popularity. In this model, source data is first extracted with little to no transformation into a first set of raw datasets. The goal of these raw datasets is to effectively model an upstream source system and its data, but in a way that can scale for online analytical processing (OLAP) workloads (e.g., using columnar file formats). All data pipelines that express business-specific transformations are then executed on top of these raw datasets.

近年来，数据湖架构越来越流行。在这种模式下，源数据首先被抽取——几乎不做或只做极少转换——成为第一组原始数据集。这些原始数据集的目标是有效地对上游源系统及其数据建模，但方式要能扩展到联机分析处理（OLAP）工作负载（例如使用列式文件格式）。所有表达业务特定转换的数据管道，都在这些原始数据集之上执行。

— p.74 —

Advantages优势

This approach has several advantages over the single-stage approach, avoiding all the pitfalls listed before:

与单阶段方式相比，这种方式有若干优势，避免了前面列出的所有陷阱：

  • Scalable design. Since the data is extracted once from each source system, the additional load on the source system is drastically reduced. Further, extracted data is stored in optimized file formats on petabyte-scale storage systems (e.g., HDFS, cloud stores), which are all specifically optimized for OLAP workloads.
    可扩展的设计。由于数据从每个源系统只抽取一次，源系统上的额外负载大幅降低。此外，抽取下来的数据以优化的文件格式存储在 PB 级存储系统上（例如 HDFS、云存储），这些存储都是专门为 OLAP 工作负载优化的。
  • Standardized and schematized. During the ingestion of the raw datasets, standardization steps can be performed and a schema can be enforced on the data, which validates both structural integrity and semantics. This prevents bad data from ever making its way into the data lake.
    标准化与 schema 化。在接入原始数据集时，可以做标准化步骤，并对数据强制施加 schema，同时校验结构完整性和语义。这会阻止坏数据进入数据湖。
  • Nimble. Data engineers can develop, test, and deploy changes to transformation business logic independently, with access to large-scale parallel processing using thousands of computing cores.
    敏捷。数据工程师可以独立地开发、测试和部署转换业务逻辑的变更，并能利用数千个计算核做大规模并行处理。
  • Unlocks data. Such a data lake houses all source data together, with rich access to SQL and other tools to explore and derive business insights by joining the data and even producing derived datasets. Machine learning models have unfettered access to all of the data.
    释放数据价值。这样一个数据湖把所有源数据集中存放，可以方便地用 SQL 和其他工具来探查、通过 join 数据、甚至产出派生数据集来获得业务洞见。机器学习模型可以不受限制地访问所有数据。

Implementation落地实现

Here are a few tips for implementing the data lake architecture, based on lessons learned from actually building large data lakes:

下面是基于实际构建大型数据湖的经验总结出的落地建议：

  • Consider ingesting databases in an incremental fashion by using change-capture systems or even approaches based on Java Database Connectivity, or JDBC (e.g., Apache Sqoop), to improve data freshness as well as further reduce load on the databases.
    考虑用增量方式接入数据库：使用变更捕获系统，甚至基于 Java 数据库连接（JDBC）的方式（例如 Apache Sqoop），以提高数据新鲜度，并进一步减轻数据库负载。
  • Standardize event streams from applications and such database change streams into a single event bus (e.g., Apache Kafka, Apache Pulsar).
    把来自应用的事件流和这类数据库变更流，标准化到一个统一事件总线（例如 Apache Kafka、Apache Pulsar）。
— p.75 —
  • Ingest the raw datasets from the event bus by using technologies that can support upserts to compact database changes into a snapshot (e.g., Apache Kudu, Apache Hudi, Apache Hive ACID).
    用支持 upsert 的技术从事件总线接入原始数据集，把数据库变更压缩成快照（例如 Apache Kudu、Apache Hudi、Apache Hive ACID）。
  • Design the raw datasets to support efficient retrieval of new records (similar to change capture) by either partitioning your data (e.g., using Apache Hive metastore) or using a system that supports change streams (e.g., Apache Hudi).
    把原始数据集设计成支持高效检索新记录（类似于变更捕获）：要么对数据做分区（例如用 Apache Hive metastore），要么使用支持变更流的系统（例如 Apache Hudi）。

1 I am part of the PPMC of Apache Hudi, as well as its cocreator.

注 1：作者是 Apache Hudi PPMC 成员，也是其联合创始人。

— p.76 —

29. Embracing Data Silos拥抱数据孤岛

Bin Fan and Amelia Wong

范斌、黄 Amella

Working in the big data and machine learning space, we frequently hear from data engineers that the biggest obstacle to extracting value from data is being able to access the data efficiently. Data silos, isolated islands of data, are often viewed by data engineers as the key culprit. Over the years, many attempts have arisen to resolve the challenges caused by data silos, but those attempts have often resulted in even more data silos. Rather than attempting to eliminate data silos, we believe the right approach is to embrace them.

在大数据和机器学习领域工作，我们经常听到数据工程师说：从数据中提取价值的最大障碍是无法高效访问数据。数据孤岛——一座座孤立的数据岛——常被数据工程师视为罪魁祸首。多年来，出现过很多解决数据孤岛问题的尝试，但这些尝试往往造出了更多孤岛。与其试图消灭数据孤岛，我们认为正确的做法是拥抱它们。

Why Data Silos Exist数据孤岛为何存在

Data silos exist for three main reasons. First, within any organization there is data with varying characteristics (Internet of Things data, behavioral data, transactional data, etc.) that is intended for different uses, and some of that data will be more business-critical than others. This drives the need for disparate storage systems. Second, history has shown that every 5 to 10 years a new wave in storage technologies churns out storage systems that are faster, cheaper, or better designed for certain types of data. Organizations also have a desire to avoid vendor lock-ins and as a result will diversify their data storage. Third, regulations mandate the siloing of data.

数据孤岛存在主要有三个原因。第一，任何组织内部都有特征各异的数据（物联网数据、行为数据、交易数据等），用于不同用途，其中一些数据比另一些更关乎业务关键。这就驱动了对不同存储系统的需求。第二，历史表明每 5 到 10 年，存储技术就会掀起新浪潮，造出更快、更便宜、或为某类数据设计得更好的存储系统。组织也希望避免厂商锁定，因此会让数据存储多元化。第三，法规要求数据必须隔离。

Embracing Data Silos拥抱数据孤岛

We believe data silos in themselves are not the challenge. The fundamental challenge is how to make data accessible to data engineers without creating more complexity or duplication. Instead of eliminating silos, we propose leveraging a data orchestration system, which sits between computing frameworks and storage systems, to resolve data access challenges. We define a data orchestration system as a layer that abstracts data access across storage systems, virtualizes all the data, and presents the data via standardized APIs with a global namespace to data-driven applications.

我们认为数据孤岛本身并不是挑战。根本的挑战是：如何在不制造更多复杂度或冗余的前提下，让数据工程师能访问数据。我们不主张消灭孤岛，而主张利用数据编排系统——它位于计算框架和存储系统之间——来解决数据访问难题。我们把数据编排系统定义为这样一层：它抽象跨存储系统的数据访问、把所有数据虚拟化、并通过带全局命名空间的标准化 API，把数据呈现给数据驱动型应用。

With a data orchestration system, data engineers can easily access data stored across various storage systems. For example, a data engineer may need to join two tables originally stored in two different regions—a local Hadoop cluster and a remote Hadoop cluster. By implementing a data orchestration system, they can address both locations from a single logical endpoint, simplifying the task of working across disparate systems. Many data orchestration systems (e.g., Alluxio) provide advanced caching capabilities, reducing the performance impact of repeated queries against the source locations. Furthermore, storage teams can make the best storage-purchasing decisions without being shackled by the impact of their decisions on application teams.

有了数据编排系统，数据工程师可以轻松访问散落在各种存储系统中的数据。例如，数据工程师可能需要 join 两张原本存在于两个不同地域的表——一个本地 Hadoop 集群和一个远程 Hadoop 集群。通过实现数据编排系统，他们可以从一个逻辑端点同时访问两个位置，简化跨异构系统的工作。许多数据编排系统（例如 Alluxio）提供高级缓存能力，减少对源位置重复查询的性能开销。此外，存储团队可以做出最佳的存储采购决策，而不必被“决策对应用团队的影响”所束缚。

— p.77 —
— p.78 —

30. Engineering Reproducible Data Science Projects工程化可复现的数据科学项目

Dr. Tianhui Michael Li

李天惠 博士

Just like any scientific field, data science is built on reproducibility. In a reproducible project, someone else (including the future you) can re-create your results by running a simple command. On the one hand, this means that you should check your analysis code into a source-control tool like Git. On the other, it also means following DevOps best practices like including dependency lists in machine-readable forms (like requirements.txt for pip or environment.yml for Conda). You might go one step further and use a Dockerfile. The commands needed to install and run the analysis should also be included. Finally, make sure that you clearly document what to run in a README.md file, or preferably in a job runner like Make.

和任何科学领域一样，数据科学建立在可复现性之上。在一个可复现的项目里，别人（包括未来的你自己）只需运行一条简单命令就能重现你的结果。一方面，这意味着你应该把分析代码签入 Git 这类源码控制工具。另一方面，这也意味着遵循 DevOps 最佳实践，比如以机器可读的形式附带依赖清单（pip 的 requirements.txt 或 Conda 的 environment.yml）。你还可以更进一步，用一个 Dockerfile。安装和运行分析所需的命令也应包括在内。最后，确保你在 README.md 中清楚记录要运行什么——更好的是放在像 Make 这样的任务运行器里。

Another important piece of reproducibility is eliminating something we'll call algorithmic randomness from your pipeline in order to maintain consistency. If your data is being subsetted from a larger dataset or your analysis depends on an initial random condition (many of your favorite ones do), you're depending on a random number generator. This can cause the same analysis to yield different results—so make sure your generator is tied to a random seed that's checked into version control. This ensures that your work can be reproduced, and any variation in your results can be attributed to the code or data, not to chance.

可复现性的另一个重要组成部分，是从管道中消除我们称之为“算法随机性”的东西，以保持一致性。如果你的数据是从更大数据集中切出来的子集，或者你的分析依赖一个初始随机条件（你喜欢的许多分析都是如此），你就在依赖一个随机数生成器。这会导致同一份分析产出不同结果——所以请确保你的生成器绑定到一个签入版本控制的随机种子。这能保证你的工作可以被复现，结果中的任何差异都可以归因于代码或数据，而不是运气。

If you work in Python, Jupyter notebooks can combine code, visualizations, and explanations in a single document. In the academic world, Nobel Prize winners have used notebooks to demonstrate the existence of gravitational waves. In industry, companies like Netflix use notebook templates to deliver visualizations to stakeholders. Don't be afraid to check notebooks into Git—Netflix does it, and so do we! We restart the kernel and rerun all the analysis from scratch before saving the output, which avoids out-of-order execution mistakes and helps guarantee that we'll get the same results the next time we run it.

如果你用 Python，Jupyter notebook 可以把代码、可视化和解释组合在一个文档里。在学术界，诺贝尔奖得主曾用 notebook 来证明引力波的存在。在工业界，像 Netflix 这样的公司用 notebook 模板向业务方交付可视化。别怕把 notebook 签入 Git——Netflix 这么做，我们也这么做！我们在保存输出前会重启内核、从头重跑整个分析，这能避免乱序执行错误，并帮助保证下次运行时得到同样的结果。

— p.79 —

Finally, it's always smart to begin a data science project with some idea of how it will be put into production. For instance, designing a pipeline that uses the same data format during the research and production phases will prevent bugs and data corruption issues later. For the same reason, it's also a good idea to sort out how your research code can be put into production before you start, rather than creating separate code for the latter.

最后，在开始一个数据科学项目时，对“它将来如何上生产”有一些想法总是明智的。例如，设计一条在研究阶段和生产阶段都使用相同数据格式的管道，可以避免日后的 bug 和数据损坏问题。出于同样的原因，在动手之前就理清研究代码如何上生产，也是个好主意，而不是到时候再另写一套代码。

When starting off as a data engineer, it's tempting to dive into what you see as the "cutting edge" of the field. But based on our experience, it's a much better investment to focus on the foundations and make sure you can create reproducible, consistent, and production-ready pipelines that are easily accessible to various stakeholders. Though it may not seem as glamorous at first, it will pay dividends over the life of both your project and your career.

刚入行做数据工程师时，你很容易一头扎进你眼中的“前沿”。但根据我们的经验，专注于基础是好得多的投资：确保你能创建可复现、一致、可上生产、并被各方利益相关者轻松访问的管道。虽然起初看起来不那么光鲜，但在你项目和职业生涯的整个生命周期里，它都会带来回报。
